title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
abstract: arXiv:2610.19121v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose \textit{LayerTrim}, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On \texttt{Qwen3-14B}, LayerTrim achieves 1.24$\times$ faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability

translated_title: 通过保持注意力的MLP裁剪解锁推理语言模型的结构化剪枝
translated_abstract: 结构化剪枝通过移除模型组件来生成更小的稠密模型，从而降低大语言模型的推理成本。然而，现有方法可能导致在AIME等长篇推理任务上的推理性能崩溃。我们提出了LayerTrim，这是一种免训练的结构化剪枝方法，它识别冗余的解码器层，并选择性地裁剪其MLP特征，同时保留注意力机制和解码器深度。LayerTrim是首个无需梯度或恢复训练即可保持长篇推理能力的免训练结构化剪枝方法。在三个推理语言模型和五个基准测试上，LayerTrim在大多数评估设置中优于现有的结构化剪枝方法，相比RESP平均准确率提升最高达21.4个百分点。在Qwen3-14B上，LayerTrim相比稠密模型实现了1.24倍的预填充加速和19.7%的峰值GPU内存降低，同时更好地保留了推理能力。
tldr: LayerTrim是一种免训练的结构化剪枝方法，通过识别冗余解码器层并选择性裁剪其MLP特征、同时保留注意力机制和解码器深度，在无需梯度或恢复训练的情况下保持长篇推理能力，相比RESP平均准确率最高提升21.4个百分点，并实现1.24倍的预填充加速和19.7%的GPU峰值内存降低。
en_tdlr: LayerTrim is a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth, maintaining long-form reasoning ability without gradients or recovery training, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP and achieving 1.24× faster prefill with 19.7% lower peak GPU memory.
